3I/ATLAS: a 3D solar-wind reconstruction

', + f'

Author: Codex-root with Codex observation, external-model and solver sub-agents. Generated {datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()}.

', + f'

{stage} The reference run {esc(best)} gives PN-good-time-weighted proton density {f(v["n"])} cm⁻³, heliocentric speed {f(v["v"])} km/s, and incident proton flux {f(v["f_incident"])} cm⁻² s⁻¹. These are model-dependent estimates, not measurements at the comet.

', + '

Time-series chart · Numerical time series · Top-down animation · Stream-contrast animation · Machine-readable results · Reproduction guide

', + '', + '

Epoch, frame and incident flux

', + '

The published pointing sequence spans 2025-12-03 12:37:38 to 2025-12-04 17:22:29 UTC. The existing analysis_06 bounds, 12:04:07 to 10:11:54 the next day, describe retained frame metadata rather than accepted science exposure. The 45 accepted PN intervals instead begin at 13:04:03.002 and end at 09:56:03.002, totaling 21,362.284 s. All quoted exposure-weighted means integrate the model over these exact intervals. GTIs and original FITS paths; evidence report.

', + '

The mesh uses the fixed solar equator and the ascending node on the J2000 ecliptic as longitude zero. Full geometric JPL Horizons vectors use UTC explicitly. Carrington maps rotate at 14.1844° per day; their phase is anchored by GONG sub-Earth longitude and the actual Earth vector. The independent IAU phase differs by only 0.169°, while per-map phase residuals reach 0.731°. WSA map orientation was checked against the original magnetogram (correlation 0.9855); treating the generic DU documentation as the exact GONG pixel origin would be incorrect here. Independent phase audit; pixel check.

', + '

The ordinary heliocentric flux is F=nₚ|vSW|. The physically incident flux used in the final flux chart is Fincident=nₚ|vSW−vcomet|. The comet moves outward at about 43 km/s radially and 66 km/s in total, so the distinction is several percent to approximately 10%. Both fluxes and both speeds are retained in the CSV. No spacecraft was treated as being co-located with the comet.

', + '

Inputs and physical closure

', + '

The solar input is 25 actual daily WSA 5.4 maps, driven by GONGZ photospheric magnetograms, from November 10 through December 4. WSA supplies radial field and empirical speed at 21.5 solar radii (0.099985 AU). Its coronal calculation uses PFSS and a Schatten current-sheet extension; this project implements the heliospheric MHD stage, rather than rebuilding that upstream coronal model. Official WSA model description; retrieval URLs and hashes.

', + f'

Pre-epoch STEREO-A and Solar Orbiter measurements over November 10–24 set instrument-balanced density, magnetic and thermal normalizations. Wind is entirely held out. The calibrated boundary uses n₄₀₀={f(m["density_1au_at400_cm3"])} cm⁻³ at 1 AU, T₄₀₀={f(m["proton_temperature_01au_at400_K"])} K at the inner boundary, and a WSA field multiplier {f(m["WSA_Br_multiplier"])}. Constant momentum flux sets n∝v⁻² and constant thermal pressure sets T∝v². Pressure is 2nₚkBTₚ, assuming equal electron and proton temperatures. The chosen WSA-to-MHD speed reduction is 50 km/s; it is tested as an uncertain model choice, not represented as the exact ENLIL boundary transformation.

', + '

STEREO-A is only about 1.1° away from the comet in solar latitude; Solar Orbiter is about 15.9° away. Their training density-normalization medians differ substantially (6.05 versus 11.25 cm⁻³), motivating separate low/high-density experiments. Spacecraft normalization does not recover the neutral coma, heavy-ion charge states or a unique unobserved density map. A prior heavy-ion fraction 3×10⁻⁴–10⁻³ could be applied to proton flux conditionally, but it is not a contemporaneous heavy-ion measurement.

', + '

Leading-order source ranking is: magnetogram-driven coronal speed/field maps; native plasma density, velocity, magnetic field and temperature; and coronagraph/CME constraints. F10.7 is useful activity context but is not a local density or ion-composition measurement. LASCO imagery and the frozen DONKI-derived cone catalogue were inspected; the selected reviewer model changes comet flux by only about 1% at most between CME and ambient runs during the PN window. Omitting explicit CME injection is conditional on that result and does not exclude missed or misdirected transients. Remote-sensing research and primary sources.

', + '

Numerical implementation and tests

', + '

The C++17 solver evolves mass, three Cartesian momentum components, total energy, three magnetic components and a GLM cleaning variable in all three spatial directions. Exact integrated spherical face-area vectors handle geometry; MC-limited MUSCL reconstruction, a Rusanov flux and SSPRK2 advance the solution. Solar gravity is included. The main closure γ=1.5 represents effective distributed heating; γ=5/3 is a sensitivity experiment, not an exact reproduction of ENLIL’s explicit heating. Radial boundaries are imposed wind/outflow, longitude is periodic, and latitude boundaries extrapolate spherical components. Rejected high-order steps use a recorded first-order fallback; no hidden density or pressure floors are used. Solver equations and implementation.

', + '

The production shell reaches 2.3 AU. Low-resolution experiments preceded refinements. Both ±30° and ±60° latitude domains were tested because radial superfast flow does not remove transverse causal communication. At the inner boundary the characteristic fast speed is a substantial fraction of radial speed, so a narrow angular wedge requires an explicit domain test.

', + f'

Uniform Cartesian MHD is preserved to float-output precision. The cold radial mass-flux errors decrease 1.235% → 0.331% → 0.104%. The Brio–Wu shock tube keeps normal field exactly constant and density L1 error against a 1600-cell reference decreases 0.01358 → 0.005794 at 400 → 800 cells. Synthetic fast/slow streams develop nonradial flow while remaining positive. These verify numerical behavior; self-comparison against a fine reference does not constitute an independent exact MHD Riemann solution. Test metrics; Canonical Brio–Wu definition.

', + '

Refinement, domain and additional-physics checks

', + f'

Criteria were recorded before reviewing production refinements: maximum pointwise differences ≤10% for density and flux, ≤5% for speed; halving the timestep should change each by ≤1%. Current Boolean results: {esc(statuses)}. These tests cover the complete published interval. A pass establishes adequate resolution only for the chosen macroscopic inputs and numerical method.

', + table(['Comparison','Max density Δ','Max speed Δ','Max heliocentric flux Δ'],comparisonrows), + '

Latitude-width experiments must be interpreted separately from cell-resolution experiments. The early coarse ±30°/±60° comparison changes flux by approximately 14%; that is measured sensitivity, not a validated ±14% uncertainty bound. Comparisons of different numerical fluxes also need to remain separate from domain comparisons. Exact-GLM preprocessing with the original dissipation changes the coarse PN flux by less than 1%, whereas a split GLM treatment with lower transverse dissipation can change it much more. This numerical-method dependence must not be hidden behind a single successful refinement test. Full divergence and scheme diagnostics; independent domain assessment.

', + '

GLM cleaning leaves nonzero magnetic divergence. The medium comet-neighborhood h|div B|/|B| decreases from about 0.018 to 0.006, and its nearest-cell value is about 0.003. A monopole-force scale is small relative to bulk inertia, but that ratio is not a rigorous accumulated-flux error bound. These calculations do not establish a converged magnetic topology. Coarse controls below quantify changing B, temperature, speed, density and γ; they are sensitivity experiments with the same coarse grid, not uncertainty percentiles.

', + table(['Control versus coarse','Max density Δ','Max speed Δ','Max flux Δ'],physicalrows), + '

Resolution/timestep chart · Original criteria · All detailed metrics

', + '

Native observations and the reviewer’s model

', + '

Native spacecraft comparisons use November 25 onward, with no Parker time mapping, fitted phase shift or amplitude tuning. This tests the model at actual measurement positions rather than using mapped observations at the unmeasured comet. The amplitude calibration improves density/flux relative to the reviewer’s uncalibrated ENLIL run, while temporal correlations and peaks remain imperfect. Spatially separated monitor residuals cannot be converted directly into a calibrated comet confidence interval. Exact metrics and coverage.

', + '', + '

The downloaded reviewer run is Jan_Deca_120925_SH_1, ENLIL 2.8f-beta, WSA 5.4/GONGZ, 576×24×90 over 0.1–3.1 AU and ±48°, with 64 selected cone CMEs. Its original analysis_06-window medians at the comet are n≈1.05 cm⁻³, |v|≈406.7 km/s, F≈4.27×10⁷ cm⁻² s⁻¹. The exact processed boundary was unavailable because the 1.15 GB bnd.nc exceeded the archive download cap. Thus this is a same-event comparison with related solar inputs, not a bitwise or physics-identical replication of ENLIL. Its historical native-probe density bias and weak correlations make it an external model, not ground truth. Original run.

', + table(['Case','PN n (cm⁻³)','PN |v| (km/s)','PN |v−vc| (km/s)','PN F (10⁷ cm⁻²s⁻¹)','PN incident F (10⁷ cm⁻²s⁻¹)'],rows), + '

Animations

', + '

The main animation maps absolute heliocentric proton flux on the J2000 ecliptic plane, interpolated from the 3D solution; it does not replace the comet’s actual out-of-plane probe. Markers are projected, with Horizons spacecraft/comet positions and Astropy builtin planet ephemerides. The extra contrast animation multiplies flux by (r/AU)² to remove radial dilution and reveal stream evolution; its colorbar explicitly labels that transformation.

', + '', + '

Resources, provenance and reproducibility

', + f'

Project elapsed time at report generation: {elapsed/60:.1f} minutes. Completed result runs use {cpu_total/60:.1f} CPU minutes in total, with largest measured per-run peak RSS {peak:.1f} MB. Concurrent wall times are not summed into project elapsed time. Experiments and interrupted runs are separately preserved; the CPU figure is therefore a documented subtotal. Latest tool-reported token counter: {token}. Token counts are not a provider billing audit.

', + '

Each solver run uses at most two threads and nice +15. The runner caps virtual memory at 1536 MB, normal CPU time at 1800 s and normal wall time at 900 s; the wider fine run has a documented 2400 s CPU cap and 1200 s wall cap. The solver itself guards array allocations at 700 MB. Independent runs can overlap while staying small relative to the 24 GB workstation. Monitoring samples machine/process use and new collaborator notes every 20 seconds. No CUDA jobs were launched by Codex.

', + table(['Run','Wall s','CPU s','Peak RSS MB','Steps','1st-order fallbacks','Weighted h divB/B'],resources), + '

All work and frozen inputs are contained here, with timestamped agent-identified notes in ../shared_notes. The README and Makefile reproduce the package offline using the recorded Python packages, GCC/OpenMP and ffmpeg. Upstream manuscripts and reduction products were read only. Source hashes, exact configuration files, standard output, resource logs, original downloaded profiles and small input maps are preserved.

', + '

Monitoring summary · Continuous resource log · Token snapshots · External source manifest · Observation manifest

', + ''] + (ROOT/'report.html').write_text('\n'.join(parts)+'\n') + print('Wrote report.html and monitoring/summary.json') + +if __name__=='__main__':main() *** End Patch"));

# BRIO: Bringing Order to Abstractive Summarization

This repo contains the code, data and trained models for our paper BRIO: Bringing Order to Abstractive Summarization.

## Quick Links

  * Overview
  * How to Install
  * Description of Codes
    * Workspace
  * Preprocessing
    * Preprocessed Data
    * Generate Candidate Summaries
    * Preprocess Your Own Data
  * How to Run
    * Hyper-parameter Setting
    * Train
    * Evaluate
  * Results, Outputs, Checkpoints
  * Use BRIO with Huggingface

## Overview

We present a novel training paradigm for neural abstractive summarization. Instead of using MLE training alone, we introduce a contrastive learning component, which encourages the abstractive models to estimate the probability of system-generated summaries more accurately.

## How to Install

  * `python3.8`
  * `conda create --name env --file spec-file.txt`
  * Further steps
    * install additional libraries (after activating the conda env) `pip install -r requirements.txt`
    * `compare_mt` -> https://github.com/neulab/compare-mt
        
        git clone https://github.com/neulab/compare-mt.git
        cd ./compare-mt
        pip install -r requirements.txt
        python setup.py install

Our code is based on Huggingface's Transformers library.

## Description of Codes

  * `cal_rouge.py` -> ROUGE calculation
  * `config.py` -> model configuration
  * `data_utils.py` -> dataloader
  * `label_smoothing_loss.py` -> label smoothing loss
  * `main.py` -> training and evaluation procedure
  * `model.py` -> models
  * `modeling_bart.py`, `modeling_pegasus.py` -> modified from Transformers library to support more efficient training
  * `preprocess.py` -> data preprocessing
  * `utils.py` -> utility functions
  * `gen_candidate.py` -> generate candidate summaries

### Workspace

Following directories should be created for our experiments.

  * `./cache` -> storing model checkpoints
  * `./result` -> storing evaluation results

## Preprocessing

We use the following datasets for our experiments.

  * CNN/DailyMail -> https://github.com/abisee/cnn-dailymail
  * XSum -> https://github.com/EdinburghNLP/XSum
  * NYT -> https://catalog.ldc.upenn.edu/LDC2008T19

### Preprocessed Data

You can download the preprocessed data for our experiments on CNNDM, CNNDM (cased) and XSum.

After donwloading, you should unzip the zip files in this root directory.

Notes: after the data preprocessing, you should also put the raw file `test.source`, `test.target` into the created data folder (e.g. `./cnndm/diverse/test.source`)

We use the PTB tokenizer provided by Standford CoreNLP (download here). Please note that tokenized texts are only used for evaluation. To tokenize a file, you may run (using test.source as an example)
    
    export CLASSPATH=/your_path/stanford-corenlp-3.8.0.jar
    cat test.source | java edu.stanford.nlp.process.PTBTokenizer -ioFileList -preserveLines > test.source.tokenized

We have provided the examples files in `./examples/raw_data`.

The preprocessing procedure will store the processed data as seperate json files in `tgt_dir`.

#### Example: preprocessing test set on CNNDM
    
    # starting from the root directory
    
    # create folders
    mkdir ./cnndm
    mkdir ./cnndm/diverse
    mkdir ./cnndm/diverse/test
    
    # suppose that the raw files are at ./raw_data, the results will be saved at ./cnndm/diverse/test
    # please remember to put the source file and the target file on test set into the folder, e.g. ./cnndm/diverse/test.source
    
    python preprocess.py --src_dir ./raw_data --tgt_dir ./cnndm/diverse --split test --cand_num 16 --dataset cnndm -l

    
    # write the system-generated files to a file: ./result/cnndm/test.out
    python main.py --cuda --gpuid 0 --config cnndm -e --model_pt cnndm/model_generation.bin -g
    
    # tokenize the output file -> ./result/cnndm/test.out.tokenized (you may use other tokenizers)
    export CLASSPATH=/your_path/stanford-corenlp-3.8.0.jar
    cat ./result/cnndm/test.out | java edu.stanford.nlp.process.PTBTokenizer -ioFileList -preserveLines > ./result/cnndm/test.out.tokenized
    
    # calculate the ROUGE scores using ROUGE Perl Package
    python cal_rouge.py --ref ./cnndm/test.target.tokenized --hyp ./result/cnndm/test.out.tokenized -l
    
    # calculate the ROUGE scores using ROUGE Python Implementation
    python cal_rouge.py --ref ./cnndm/test.target.tokenized --hyp ./result/cnndm/test.out.tokenized -l -p

#### Example: evaluating the model as a scorer on CNNDM
    
    # rerank the candidate summaries
    python main.py --cuda --gpuid 0 --config cnndm -e --model_pt cnndm/model_ranking.bin -r
    
    # calculate the ROUGE scores using ROUGE Perl Package
    # ./result/cnndm/reference and ./result/cnndm/candidate are two folders containing files. Each one of those files contain one summary
    python cal_rouge.py --ref ./result/cnndm/reference --hyp ./result/cnndm/candidate -l
    
    # calculate the ROUGE scores using ROUGE Python Implementation
    # ./result/cnndm/reference and ./result/cnndm/candidate are two folders containing files. Each one of those files contain one summary
    python cal_rouge.py --ref ./result/cnndm/reference --hyp ./result/cnndm/candidate -l -p

% cd bin
